title: October 27 — Berglund cavities, OpenAI wave filtering, and writable-wall memory
summary: Six source-curated nodes: add the previously unreviewed June ResonantNeuron precursor and five October 27 paper-adjacent repos. Nils Berglund-inspired interference computation branches into persistent Robin wall memory, geometry-limited scattering calibration, directional image decomposition, controlled physical incident probes, and a separate four-record questioning needle. K24 stadium confirms the geometry/amplitude pruning rule in simulation; the parabolic incident source and adaptive needle both fail superior-control gates. OpenAI's new Euclidean local-smoothing theorem is inspiration only, not a proof for any inverse memory or learning result.

nodes.claim: June 2026 Berglund-inspired resonator computer: skewed satellite-cavity dendrites feed an interference soma with a threshold axon. Phase-coded resonator gates compose into a full adder; later V11–V18 explorations confront real-wave and hard-boundary effects.
nodes.survived: Original source reports XOR from a phasor magnitude-band primitive, 8/8 full-adder truth rows, 1000/1000 algebraic and 60/60 dynamical ripple-add trials; its later V-series separates lumped oscillator computation from harder physical wave propagation and writes down failures.
nodes.killed: The original logic bands, weights, and gate targets were designed, not learned. A resonant gate is not an experience-written persistent cavity wall or evidence for cortical arithmetic; later real-wave variants do not turn the original arithmetic demonstration into a biological mechanism.
nodes.era: October 27: from Berglund cavities to paper-inspired memory interrogation

nodes.claim: Uses the October 25 OpenAI Euclidean-wave paper's frequency-dependent angular multiplier as a source of testable hypotheses for lossless oriented Sihti image residues; compares parabolic, fixed8, sp8, anti-parabolic, isotropic and ray windows under a coefficient budget.
nodes.survived: BSDS500 200-image preregistered test: parabolic beats fixed8 on G4 at 10% budget (145/200 images) and the implemented sp8 angular control (171/200). Coherence ranking concentrates retained energy near human boundaries (148/200) but reduces G4 region alignment.
nodes.killed: Paper-derived ray window does not outperform stepwise parabolic windows (82/200). Parabolic-vs-fixed8 at equal PSNR is not significant under declared gate (112/200), and isotropic Sihti wins the main G4 comparison (169/200 against parabolic). The tested sp8 is a steerable-style control, not an independent complete stock steerable-pyramid benchmark. No OpenAI theorem about image recognition is established.

nodes.claim: Eight externally written Robin boundary springs store bits independently of fleeting wave amplitudes in a damped elliptical cavity. Signed echo probes test whether the receiver can identify the written pattern and which higher-order wall interactions are necessary.
nodes.survived: Eight-patch experiments recover individually written changes; fourth-order inclusion–exclusion model decodes 93/93 held-out five-or-more-bit states under specified calibration and noise conditions after measuring 163 of 256 configurations per source. Multi-patch echoes exhibit non-additive material interaction even with a linear fixed-wall wave PDE.
nodes.killed: One-wall additive templates do not recover the multiwall memories (0/12 in the reported control). Persistence is imposed, not learned plasticity; the OpenAI imaginary-ray filter does not automatically improve directional readout or establish a theorem for a bounded reflecting cavity.
nodes.era: October 27: from Berglund cavities to paper-inspired memory interrogation

nodes.claim: Derives a geometry-dependent causal-tour selection of writable-wall interaction subsets: calibrate interactions whose source→patches→receiver scattering tours can arrive in the listening window; an amplitude-pruning rule further cuts the calibration cost.
nodes.survived: K16 preregistration confirms safe tour/onset bounds but rejects an overly expensive whole-order ceiling. Post-hoc K16 sparse sets use 219 states for 300/300 heldouts. A separate preregistered K24 Bunimovich stadium test reports 300/300 correct at noise with 7,164 per-subset tour calibrations; an ellipse-trained amplitude-pruned 848-state model also scores 300/300 from 16,777,216 possible 24-bit wall states, with explicit inactive-set controls and transferred amplitude correlation r=0.92.
nodes.killed: A fixed interaction order is an over-costly bound (K16 needed only degree 2 rather than presumed 4–6). The sharper per-subset and amplitude laws were discovered post hoc before stadium confirmation. Calibration was still externally designed and simulated; these numerical findings are not a universal physical-memory capacity theorem nor a rule for learning wall writes.

nodes.claim: Browser physical-interrogation labs progress from four externally writable wall bits to eight-bit sparse calibration, then physically launch equal-energy directional packets using the OpenAI paper's parabolic angular weighting and compare with fixed-angle sources in held-out cavities.
nodes.survived: The physical one-cell receiver and blind memory tasks separate stored wall changes from resonance itself. Directional waveform shapes genuinely change source/receiver traces; a frozen original-ellipse tuning selects conventional fixed q=0.45 before validation on a stadium and +25° rotated ellipse, with 37 calibration patterns and two equal-energy pings.
nodes.killed: Across 657 paired noisy trials in each unfamiliar geometry, parabolic packets lose to the tuned fixed-width baseline: stadium 51.1% vs 70.8%, rotated ellipse 34.7% vs 42.2%. One-frequency parabolic vs arbitrary fixed q had an exact matched-width control; its earlier favorable comparisons cannot establish general superiority. No local-smoothing bound transfers to the reflecting/damped cavity.

nodes.claim: Static browser bank of four learned 2×2 transformation records. An active questioning needle can purchase extra diagnostic observations to infer the hidden switching rule before predicting; compares feedback-only, random, fixed and disagreement-adaptive queries in five synthetic worlds.
nodes.survived: Across 20 paired directional-world seeds, questioning reduces charged prediction loss 23.4% relative to ordinary feedback-only tracking; records, probe choices and costs are inspectable. Five-world benchmark and nine engine tests are published with JSON export.
nodes.killed: The adaptive needle fails the preregistered superiority criterion: charged loss 0.012974 versus 0.012671 for fixed probe (2.4% worse), losing to fixed on all 20 seeds; fast switching is worse. Records were trained on identified examples and frozen for evaluation. No direct OpenAI wave local-smoothing mechanism or learned cavity wall exists here.

edges.why: Kavitaatio is explicitly inspired by the resonant-cavity/neuron question, but replaces designed interference gates with an externally writable reflecting-wall material state. Conceptual lineage; no code fork or biological learning asserted.
ParabolicOrientationSihti explicitly extends Sihti's exact core+residue reconstruction and G4 analysis by splitting octave residues into angular components informed by the 2026 OpenAI paper.

WallMemoryLaw explicitly reuses the same eight-patch material-interaction wave solver and turns the listening deadline into a causal calibration-selection rule, later testing K16 and an unfamiliar K24 stadium.

The browser interrogation laboratory states it derives its elliptical wave model and persistent Robin springs from Kavitaatio, adding physical source comparisons, hidden-word scoring and geometry tests.

Both investigate geometry-limited calibration under finite wave travel times; the browser eight-bit experiment separately compares causal tour selection with degree-first control. Neither proves the other's universal law.
BigKahuna explicitly starts with Kahuna's four separately learned records and needle metaphor, then freezes records to isolate which additional probing strategy reduces prediction loss.

The cavity and switching-record environments independently expose that a smart-looking adaptive query need not beat a tuned fixed readout; this is conceptual comparison, not direct code or theorem inheritance.

motifs.title: A memory is the changed material, not the echo
motifs.description: ResonantNeuron's interference gates motivated the question, Kavitaatio separates a persistent externally written Robin wall from transient wave excitation, and WallMemoryLaw exploits how repeated scatterings from those wall changes become measurable. The missing mechanism is experience-dependent wall writing rather than another focusing picture.

motifs.title: A beautiful Fourier multiplier is not a better memory probe by decree
motifs.description: The October 25 OpenAI Euclidean local-smoothing paper supplies the imaginary-ray directional multiplier motivating the Sihti image tests and physical incident packets. Conventional curvelet-style parabolic scaling already exists; the paper's specific ray window does not beat stepwise parabolic Sihti, and tuned fixed-width packets beat paper-inspired packets in two independent cavity geometries. Mathematical free-space bounds do not prove inverse memory accuracy.

motifs.title: Useful interrogations require an error-based control
motifs.description: WallMemoryLaw's causal-set selection, the real wave receiver, and the four-record BigKahuna questioning needle show why selecting the strongest focus or greatest response disagreement is not the same as minimizing confusion between memories. A calibrated fixed probe can beat adaptive source selection; prediction risk, calibration budget, and measurement cost must be explicitly accounted for.
